title: AI Model Architecture Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Transformer, state-space, graph, multimodal, and emerging model architectures with design records and comparisons. The AI Model Architecture Database documents neural network architectures as engineering records: the math of the layer, the compute and memory cost, the training behavior, and the measured results. It covers transformers, state-space models, graph networks, multimodal fusion designs, and emerging alternatives, each with a standard record format so architectures can be compared apples-to-apples instead of by marketing claim.

title: AI Model Architecture Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Core layer math. Self-attention: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V, cost O(n^2 d). State-space (S4-style): x'(t) = Ax(t) + Bu(t), y(t) = Cx(t) + Du(t), discretized to a linear recurrence, cost O(n d). Graph convolution: H' = sigma(D^-1/2 A D^-1/2 H W). Mixture-of-experts routing: y = sum_i g_i(x) E_i(x) with top-k gating. Multimodal fusion: cross-attention layers where queries come from one modality and keys/values from another. Scaling laws (empirical): loss L(N,D) ~ a*N^-alpha + b*D^-beta for parameters N and data D. Memory: activations dominate at long context; KV-cache grows O(n*d*layers) during generation.

title: AI Model Architecture Database — Execution: runnable tool
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Runnable workflow: the architecture comparator takes two architecture records and a task profile, computes theoretical FLOPs and memory from the layer formulas, runs a synthetic scaling simulation, and emits a comparison table. The shape-checker validates a layer config (dims must divide by heads, d_model consistent). Demos execute a miniature transformer forward pass and a state-space recurrence on synthetic data and compare per-token cost curves as context grows.

title: AI Model Architecture Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: formula-consistency test (reported FLOPs match the layer math within 1%); shape test (all tensor dims resolve with no mismatch); benchmark-integrity test (compared models share training budget and data); unit tests on every demo computation. Limitations: theoretical FLOPs ignore kernel efficiency; published benchmark numbers are as-reported, not independently rerun; emerging architectures have thin evidence. Records carry last-verified dates and the source of each measured number.

demo.title: Verification: calibration error (ECE)
demo.code: const pairs=[[0.9,1],[0.9,1],[0.9,0],[0.6,1],[0.6,0],[0.6,0]];const bins={};pairs.forEach(([c,ok])=>{const b=Math.round(c*10)/10;(bins[b]=bins[b]||{n:0,c:0,conf:0});bins[b].n++;bins[b].c+=ok;bins[b].conf+=c;});let ece=0;for(const b in bins){const B=bins[b];ece+=Math.abs(B.c/B.n-B.conf/B.n)*(B.n/pairs.length);}J({ece:+ece.toFixed(3)});assert(ece>0&&ece<1,'ece');
